references.observation: The authors identify the entrance building and visitor-facing miniature workshop as part of their park design.
The park-facing elevation behind the curved café terrace has dark glazed bays and small round windows. A dark metal railing runs along a blue retaining face above the exhibit water.

references.attribution: Jacob Richman, 2003 photograph of the park's visitor map
references.observation: The visitor map shows restaurant and shop symbols within the main visitor complex, behind the entrance and adjacent to the display water. The map is pictorial.
Two pointed openings cut the raised limestone front, supported on slim columns. Dark canopy members are visible beyond the wall.
The park building lies between the paved vehicle approach and miniature exhibits. The aerial shows a stepped roof outline, a raised glass block over the entry and its arched façade.

limitations: The stepped workshop outline matches the large footprint beside the information point and approach. The gate faces the visitor approach, toward the northwest. The precise opening positions, pavilion height and rear openings are reconstructed from photographs.

The retained Terrarium rises across the workshop. Stepped building volumes and buried foundation skirts follow that terrain. The entrance slab is anchored near the sampled front path. The exterior heights are approximate.

The asset represents the park’s full-size entrance, workshop and connected waterside café frontage. The roof furnishings, bay count and terrace grade are approximations. Other visitor buildings and miniature exhibits are separate components.
